methods.label: Find a right angle and a diameter
methods.explanation:
The extensions give the point orders \(P,B,A\) and \(P,C,D\). Thus \(PA=8+10=18\), and \(\angle APC=60^\circ\).

For two secants from an exterior point, the external segment times the whole secant segment is the same on both lines. Let \(PC=x>0\), so \(PD=x+7\). Then
\[
x(x+7)=PB\cdot PA=8\cdot18=144,
\]
which factors as
\[
(x-9)(x+16)=0.
\]
The negative root cannot be a length, so \(PC=9\).

Now \(PC\) is half of \(PA\), and their included angle is \(60^\circ\). To see the resulting right angle, drop a perpendicular from \(A\) to line \(PC\), with foot \(T\). The acute angle at \(P\) places \(T\) on ray \(PC\). Right triangle \(PAT\) has angles \(60^\circ\) at \(P\) and \(30^\circ\) at \(A\), so
\[
PT=\frac{PA}{2}=9=PC.
\]
Therefore \(T=C\), proving \(AC\perp CD\).

The inscribed angle \(ACD\) is consequently a right angle, so its opposite chord \(AD\) is a diameter. Applying the Pythagorean theorem twice gives
\[
AC^2=18^2-9^2=243,
\]
\[
AD^2=AC^2+CD^2=243+49=292.
\]
Since \(AD=2r\), we obtain \(r^2=292/4=\boxed{73}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
